     2	name: report-generator
     3	description: Generate professional PDF/HTML reports with charts, tables, and narrative from data. Supports templates, branding, and automated report generation.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# Report Generator
     7	
     8	Create professional, data-driven reports with charts, tables, and narrative text. Perfect for business reports, analytics dashboards, status updates, and automated reporting pipelines.
     9	
    10	## Quick Start
    11	
    12	```python
    13	from scripts.report_gen import ReportGenerator
    14	
    15	# Create a simple report
    16	report = ReportGenerator("Monthly Sales Report")
    17	report.add_text("This report summarizes sales performance for Q4 2024.")
    18	report.add_table(sales_data, title="Sales by Region")
    19	report.add_chart(sales_data, chart_type="bar", title="Revenue by Month")
    20	report.add_text("Key findings: Revenue increased 25% quarter-over-quarter.")
    21	report.generate().save("sales_report.pdf")
    22	
    23	# From template
    24	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("executive_summary")
    25	report.set_data(data_dict)
    26	report.generate().save("exec_summary.pdf")
    27	```
    28	
    29	## Features
    30	
    31	- **Multiple Output Formats**: PDF, HTML
    32	- **Rich Content**: Text, tables, charts, images, headers
    33	- **Chart Types**: Bar, line, pie, scatter, area, heatmap
    34	- **Table Formatting**: Auto-styling, conditional formatting
    35	- **Templates**: Pre-built report templates
    36	- **Branding**: Logo, colors, fonts, headers/footers
    37	- **Sections**: Table of contents, page numbers, appendices
    38	- **Data Integration**: CSV, DataFrame, dict inputs
    39	
    40	## API Reference
    41	
    42	### Initialization
    43	
    44	```python
    45	# New report
    46	report = ReportGenerator("Report Title")
    47	report = ReportGenerator("Report Title", subtitle="Q4 2024 Analysis")
    48	
    49	# From template
    50	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("quarterly_review")
    51	
    52	# With config
    53	report = ReportGenerator("Title", config={
    54	    "page_size": "letter",
    55	    "orientation": "portrait",
    56	    "margins": {"top": 1, "bottom": 1, "left": 0.75, "right": 0.75}
    57	})
    58	```
    59	
    60	### Report Metadata
    61	
    62	```python
    63	# Title and subtitle
    64	report.set_title("Annual Report 2024")
    65	report.set_subtitle("Financial Performance Analysis")
    66	
    67	# Author and date
    68	report.set_author("Analytics Team")
    69	report.set_date("December 2024")
    70	report.set_date_auto()  # Use today
    71	
    72	# Organization
    73	report.set_organization("Acme Corporation")
    74	report.set_logo("logo.png")
    75	```
    76	
    77	### Adding Content
    78	
    79	#### Text Content
    80	
    81	```python
    82	# Simple paragraph
    83	report.add_text("This is a paragraph of analysis text.")
    84	
    85	# Styled text
    86	report.add_text("Important finding!", style="highlight")
    87	report.add_text("Key metric: 42%", style="metric")
    88	
    89	# Headers
    90	report.add_heading("Executive Summary", level=1)
    91	report.add_heading("Revenue Analysis", level=2)
    92	report.add_heading("By Region", level=3)
    93	
    94	# Bullet points
    95	report.add_bullets([
    96	    "Revenue increased 25% YoY",
    97	    "Customer acquisition up 15%",
    98	    "Churn rate decreased to 3%"
    99	])
   100	
   101	# Numbered list
   102	report.add_numbered_list([
   103	    "Expand to European markets",
   104	    "Launch mobile application",
   105	    "Implement AI-driven analytics"
   106	])
   107	```
   108	
   109	#### Tables
   110	
   111	```python
   112	# From DataFrame
   113	import pandas as pd
   114	df = pd.DataFrame({
   115	    'Region': ['North', 'South', 'East', 'West'],
   116	    'Revenue': [100000, 85000, 92000, 78000],
   117	    'Growth': ['12%', '8%', '15%', '5%']
   118	})
   119	report.add_table(df, title="Regional Performance")
   120	
   121	# From dict/list
   122	data = [
   123	    {'Product': 'A', 'Sales': 1000, 'Profit': 200},
   124	    {'Product': 'B', 'Sales': 1500, 'Profit': 350}
   125	]
   126	report.add_table(data, title="Product Summary")
   127	
   128	# With styling
   129	report.add_table(df, title="Sales Data",
   130	    highlight_max=['Revenue'],       # Highlight max values
   131	    highlight_min=['Growth'],        # Highlight min values
   132	    currency_cols=['Revenue'],       # Format as currency
   133	    percent_cols=['Growth'],         # Format as percent
   134	    align={'Region': 'left', 'Revenue': 'right'}
   135	)
   136	```
   137	
   138	#### Charts
   139	
   140	```python
   141	# Bar chart
   142	report.add_chart(
   143	    data=df,
   144	    chart_type="bar",
   145	    x="Region",
   146	    y="Revenue",
   147	    title="Revenue by Region"
   148	)
   149	
   150	# Line chart
   151	report.add_chart(
   152	    data=time_series_df,
   153	    chart_type="line",
   154	    x="Month",
   155	    y=["Sales", "Forecast"],
   156	    title="Sales Trend"
   157	)
   158	
   159	# Pie chart
   160	report.add_chart(
   161	    data=category_df,
   162	    chart_type="pie",
   163	    values="Amount",
   164	    labels="Category",
   165	    title="Budget Allocation"
   166	)
   167	
   168	# Chart options
   169	report.add_chart(
   170	    data=df,
   171	    chart_type="bar",
   172	    x="Region",
   173	    y="Revenue",
   174	    title="Revenue Analysis",
   175	    color="#3498db",
   176	    width=6,           # inches
   177	    height=4,
   178	    show_values=True,
   179	    show_legend=True
   180	)
   181	```
   182	
   183	#### Images
   184	
   185	```python
   186	# Add image
   187	report.add_image("screenshot.png", caption="Dashboard View")
   188	report.add_image("diagram.png", width=5, caption="Architecture Diagram")
   189	```
   190	
   191	#### Special Elements
   192	
   193	```python
   194	# Page break
   195	report.add_page_break()
   196	
   197	# Horizontal line
   198	report.add_divider()
   199	
   200	# Spacer
   201	report.add_spacer(height=0.5)  # inches
   202	
   203	# Callout box
   204	report.add_callout(
   205	    "Key Insight: Customer retention improved 20% after implementing the new onboarding flow.",
   206	    style="info"  # info, warning, success, error
   207	)
   208	
   209	# Quote
   210	report.add_quote(
   211	    "Data is the new oil.",
   212	    attribution="Clive Humby"
   213	)
   214	```
   215	
   216	### Sections and Structure
   217	
   218	```python
   219	# Start a new section
   220	report.start_section("Financial Analysis")
   221	
   222	# Add content to section
   223	report.add_text("...")
   224	report.add_table(...)
   225	
   226	# End section
   227	report.end_section()
   228	
   229	# Table of contents (auto-generated)
   230	report.enable_toc()
   231	
   232	# Appendix
   233	report.start_appendix()
   234	report.add_heading("Raw Data", level=2)
   235	report.add_table(raw_data)
   236	```
   237	
   238	### Branding and Styling
   239	
   240	```python
   241	# Logo and organization
   242	report.set_logo("logo.png", width=150)
   243	report.set_organization("Acme Corp")
   244	
   245	# Colors
   246	report.set_colors(
   247	    primary="#1e40af",      # Headers, accents
   248	    secondary="#6b7280",    # Secondary text
   249	    background="#ffffff"    # Background
   250	)
   251	
   252	# Fonts
   253	report.set_fonts(
   254	    heading="Helvetica-Bold",
   255	    body="Helvetica"
   256	)
   257	
   258	# Header and footer
   259	report.set_header("Confidential - Internal Use Only")
   260	report.set_footer("Page {page} of {total}")
   261	
   262	# Watermark
   263	report.set_watermark("DRAFT")
   264	```
   265	
   266	### Templates
   267	
   268	```python

   270	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("executive_summary")
   271	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("quarterly_review")
   272	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("project_status")
   273	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("analytics_dashboard")

   281	    "customers": 5000,

   284	report.generate()

   286	
   287	### Generation and Export
   288	
   289	```python
   290	# Generate report
   291	report.generate()
   292	
   293	# Save as PDF
   294	report.save("report.pdf")
   295	
   296	# Save as HTML
   297	report.save("report.html")
   298	
   299	# Get bytes
   300	pdf_bytes = report.to_bytes()
   301	html_string = report.to_html()
   302	```

   334	## CLI Usage
   335	
   336	```bash
   337	# Generate from JSON config
   338	python report_gen.py --config report_config.json --output report.pdf
   339	
   340	# With template
   341	python report_gen.py --template executive_summary --data data.json --output summary.pdf
   342	
   343	# Quick report from CSV

   346	
   347	### CLI Arguments
   348	
   349	| Argument | Description | Default |
   350	|----------|-------------|---------|
   351	| `--config` | Report configuration JSON | - |
   352	| `--template` | Template name | - |
   353	| `--data` | Data JSON file | - |
   354	| `--csv` | CSV data file | - |
   355	| `--title` | Report title | `Report` |
   356	| `--output` | Output file path | `report.pdf` |
   357	| `--format` | Output format (pdf/html) | `pdf` |

1	# UK Retail Fuel Prices — Price History Dataset
     2	
     3	## About the Dataset
     4	
     5	This dataset is sourced from **Kaggle (jamesb7/fuel-prices-uk)** and provides UK retail fuel prices at an individual forecourt level, originally collected from the UK Government's official Fuel Finder API. The data is aggregated by [fuelcosts.co.uk](https://fuelcosts.co.uk), a fuel price comparison platform covering over 8,000 petrol stations across England, Scotland, and Wales.
     6	
     7	The file `price_history.csv` contains **396,502 rows** and **6 columns**. Each row represents a single fuel price observation at a specific station at a specific point in time.
     8	
     9	## Column Schema
    10	
    11	| Column Name | Type | Description |
    12	|---|---|---|
    13	| `id` | Integer | Unique auto-incrementing identifier for each price record. |
    14	| `node_id` | String | Hashed identifier for the fuel station (forecourt). Each unique value represents a distinct station. These are SHA-style hashes (64+ characters), not human-readable names. |
    15	| `fuel_type` | String | The type of fuel. Known values include: **E10** (standard unleaded petrol), **B7_STANDARD** (standard diesel), **E5** (super unleaded petrol), and potentially premium diesel variants. |
    16	| `price_pence` | Integer | The retail price of the fuel in **pence per litre (PPL)**. Whole number values (e.g., 133 means £1.33/litre). |
    17	| `recorded_at` | String (ISO 8601 datetime) | Timestamp when the price was recorded/collected into the dataset. Format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`. |
    18	| `source_updated_at` | String (ISO 8601 datetime) | Timestamp when the retailer last updated/reported this price to the government feed. Format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`. |
    19	
    20	## Key Column Details
    21	
    22	### fuel_type
    23	The dataset covers multiple fuel types mandated under the UK open data scheme:
    24	- **E10**: Standard unleaded petrol (the default grade at most UK pumps since 2021)
    25	- **B7_STANDARD**: Standard diesel (containing up to 7% biodiesel)
    26	- **E5**: Super unleaded petrol (higher octane, contains up to 5% ethanol)
    27	- Other premium or specialty fuels may also appear
    28	
    29	Not all stations sell every fuel type — some may only report E10 and B7_STANDARD.
    30	
    31	### node_id
    32	Station identifiers are anonymised hashes. Without a separate station metadata lookup table, individual station names, brands, or geographic locations cannot be determined from this file alone. However, the `node_id` can be used to group records by station and analyse per-station behaviour.
    33	
    34	### Timestamps
    35	The difference between `recorded_at` and `source_updated_at` is analytically meaningful. `source_updated_at` reflects when the retailer actually changed or confirmed their price, while `recorded_at` reflects when the data collection system captured it. The lag between these two timestamps can indicate how fresh the data is and how frequently retailers update their feeds.
    36	
    37	## Data Quality Notes
    38	
    39	- **No missing values** are apparent in the sample, but analysts should verify for nulls across the full 396,502 rows.
    40	- **Price values** are integers in pence. Typical UK fuel prices in early 2026 range roughly from 125 to 165+ pence per litre depending on fuel type and location. Outliers outside this range should be investigated.
    41	- **Timestamps** are in UTC (indicated by the `Z` suffix). All datetime parsing should account for ISO 8601 format.
    42	- The sample data is from **early February 2026**. The full dataset's date range should be confirmed during analysis.
    43	- Since station metadata (brand, address, coordinates) is not included in this CSV, geographic or brand-level analysis is not possible with this file alone.
    44	
    45	## Attribution
    46	
    47	- Data compiled by fuelcosts.co.uk
    48	- Source data: UK Government Fuel Finder scheme
    49	- License: CC BY 4.0

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from datetime import datetime

df = pd.read_csv('benchmark/data.csv')

# Clean data: remove obvious outliers (prices >400ppl or <50ppl are data errors)
df_clean = df[(df['price_pence'] >= 50) & (df['price_pence'] <= 400)].copy()
print(f"Original rows: {len(df)}, After cleaning: {len(df_clean)}, Removed: {len(df)-len(df_clean)}")

# Parse timestamps
df_clean['recorded_at_dt'] = pd.to_datetime(df_clean['recorded_at'])
df_clean['source_updated_at_dt'] = pd.to_datetime(df_clean['source_updated_at'])

# Calculate update lag in hours
df_clean['update_lag_hours'] = (df_clean['recorded_at_dt'] - df_clean['source_updated_at_dt']).dt.total_seconds() / 3600

# Handle negative lags (recorded before source update - likely clock skew)
negative_lags = df_clean['update_lag_hours'] < 0
print(f"Negative lags (clock skew): {negative_lags.sum()}")

# For analysis, use absolute value for very small negatives, flag larger ones
df_clean['update_lag_hours_adj'] = df_clean['update_lag_hours'].clip(lower=0)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import base64
from io import BytesIO

# Set professional style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams['font.family'] = 'DejaVu Sans'
plt.rcParams['font.size'] = 10
plt.rcParams['axes.titlesize'] = 12
plt.rcParams['axes.labelsize'] = 10

# Color palette - government/professional
COLORS = {
    'E10': '#1f77b4',
    'B7_STANDARD': '#ff7f0e', 
    'E5': '#2ca02c',
    'B7_PREMIUM': '#d62728',
    'B10': '#9467bd',
    'HVO': '#8c564b'
}

df = pd.read_csv('/app/output/cleaned_data.csv')
latest = df.sort_values('recorded_at').groupby(['node_id', 'fuel_type']).last().reset_index()
main_fuels = ['E10', 'B7_STANDARD', 'E5', 'B7_PREMIUM']
main_latest = latest[latest['fuel_type'].isin(main_fuels)].copy()

def fig_to_base64(fig):
    buf = BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    img_base64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode('utf-8')
    plt.close(fig)
    return img_base64

# Chart 1: Box plot - Price Distribution by Fuel Type
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
data_for_box = [main_latest[main_latest['fuel_type'] == f]['price_pence'].values for f in main_fuels]
bp = ax.boxplot(data_for_box, labels=['E10\n(Unleaded)', 'B7 Standard\n(Diesel)', 'E5\n(Super Unleaded)', 'B7 Premium\n(Diesel)'],
                patch_artist=True, showfliers=True, widths=0.6)
for patch, fuel in zip(bp['boxes'], main_fuels):
    patch.set_facecolor(COLORS[fuel])
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax.set_title('Retail Fuel Price Distribution by Fuel Type — February–April 2026')
ax.set_ylim(80, 280)
ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
# Add mean markers
for i, fuel in enumerate(main_fuels):
    mean_val = main_latest[main_latest['fuel_type'] == fuel]['price_pence'].mean()
    ax.scatter(i+1, mean_val, marker='D', color='black', s=40, zorder=5)
ax.scatter([], [], marker='D', color='black', s=40, label='Mean')
ax.legend(loc='upper right')
chart1 = fig_to_base64(fig)

# Chart 2: Violin plot for better distribution view
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
parts = ax.violinplot(data_for_box, positions=range(1, len(main_fuels)+1), showmeans=True, showmedians=True)
for i, pc in enumerate(parts['bodies']):
    pc.set_facecolor(COLORS[main_fuels[i]])
    pc.set_alpha(0.6)
parts['cmeans'].set_color('black')
parts['cmedians'].set_color('white')
parts['cmedians'].set_linewidth(2)
ax.set_xticks(range(1, len(main_fuels)+1))
ax.set_xticklabels(['E10\n(Unleaded)', 'B7 Standard\n(Diesel)', 'E5\n(Super Unleaded)', 'B7 Premium\n(Diesel)'])
ax.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax.set_title('Price Density Distribution by Fuel Type')
ax.set_ylim(80, 280)
ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
chart2 = fig_to_base64(fig)

# Chart 3: IQR and Range comparison bar chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
stats_data = []
for fuel in main_fuels:
    sub = main_latest[main_latest['fuel_type'] == fuel]['price_pence']
    stats_data.append({
        'fuel': fuel,
        'iqr': sub.quantile(0.75) - sub.quantile(0.25),
        'range': sub.max() - sub.min()
    })
stats_df = pd.DataFrame(stats_data)
x = np.arange(len(main_fuels))
width = 0.35
bars1 = ax.bar(x - width/2, stats_df['iqr'], width, label='Interquartile Range (IQR)', color='#2E86AB', alpha=0.85)
bars2 = ax.bar(x + width/2, stats_df['range'], width, label='Max – Min Range', color='#A23B72', alpha=0.85)
ax.set_ylabel('Price Spread (pence per litre)')
ax.set_title('Price Spread & Market Competitiveness by Fuel Type')
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(['E10', 'B7 Standard', 'E5', 'B7 Premium'])
ax.legend()
ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
# Add value labels
for bar in bars1:
    height = bar.get_height()
    ax.annotate(f'{height:.1f}', xy=(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, height),
                xytext=(0, 3), textcoords="offset points", ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)
for bar in bars2:
    height = bar.get_height()
    ax.annotate(f'{height:.1f}', xy=(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, height),
                xytext=(0, 3), textcoords="offset points", ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)
chart3 = fig_to_base64(fig)

# Chart 4: Update lag histogram
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
df['update_lag_hours'] = (pd.to_datetime(df['recorded_at']) - pd.to_datetime(df['source_updated_at'])).dt.total_seconds() / 3600
df['update_lag_hours_adj'] = df['update_lag_hours'].clip(lower=0)
# Cap at 168 hours (7 days) for visualization, with overflow bin
lag_capped = df['update_lag_hours_adj'].clip(upper=168)
ax.hist(lag_capped, bins=50, color='#2E86AB', edgecolor='white', alpha=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel('Update Lag (hours, capped at 168 hrs / 7 days)')
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Records')
ax.set_title('Retailer Price Reporting Freshness Distribution')
ax.axvline(df['update_lag_hours_adj'].median(), color='#d62728', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, label=f"Median: {df['update_lag_hours_adj'].median():.2f} hrs")
ax.legend()
ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
chart4 = fig_to_base64(fig)

# Chart 5: Lag by fuel type - stacked bar of categories
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
lag_cats = ['< 1 min', '1 min – 1 hr', '1–24 hrs', '1–7 days', '> 7 days']
def lag_cat(h):
    if h <= 1/60: return '< 1 min'
    elif h <= 1: return '1 min – 1 hr'
    elif h <= 24: return '1–24 hrs'
    elif h <= 168: return '1–7 days'
    else: return '> 7 days'
df['lag_cat'] = df['update_lag_hours_adj'].apply(lag_cat)
lag_pct = pd.crosstab(df['fuel_type'], df['lag_cat'], normalize='index') * 100
lag_pct = lag_pct.reindex(main_fuels)
lag_pct = lag_pct[lag_cats]  # ensure order
bottom = np.zeros(len(main_fuels))
colors_lag = ['#2ca02c', '#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#d62728', '#9467bd']
for i, cat in enumerate(lag_cats):
    ax.barh(range(len(main_fuels)), lag_pct[cat], left=bottom, color=colors_lag[i], label=cat, alpha=0.85)
    bottom += lag_pct[cat].values
ax.set_yticks(range(len(main_fuels)))
ax.set_yticklabels(['E10', 'B7 Standard', 'E5', 'B7 Premium'])
ax.set_xlabel('Percentage of Records (%)')
ax.set_title('Update Freshness by Fuel Type')
ax.legend(loc='lower right', fontsize=8)
ax.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)
chart5 = fig_to_base64(fig)

# Chart 6: Station coverage pie/donut
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
coverage = main_latest.groupby('fuel_type')['node_id'].nunique().reindex(main_fuels)
labels = ['E10\n(Unleaded)', 'B7 Standard\n(Diesel)', 'E5\n(Super Unleaded)', 'B7 Premium\n(Diesel)']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax.pie(coverage.values, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
                                   colors=[COLORS[f] for f in main_fuels],
                                   startangle=90, pctdistance=0.75,
                                   wedgeprops=dict(width=0.5, edgecolor='white'))
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')
    autotext.set_fontsize(10)
ax.set_title('Station Coverage by Fuel Type\n(Share of 7,367 Forecourts)')
chart6 = fig_to_base64(fig)

# Chart 7: Mean price trend over time (weekly)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
df['week'] = pd.to_datetime(df['recorded_at']).dt.to_period('W')
weekly = df[df['fuel_type'].isin(main_fuels)].groupby(['week', 'fuel_type'])['price_pence'].mean().reset_index()
weekly['week_dt'] = weekly['week'].dt.to_timestamp()
for fuel in main_fuels:
    sub = weekly[weekly['fuel_type'] == fuel]
    ax.plot(sub['week_dt'], sub['price_pence'], marker='o', markersize=4, label=fuel, color=COLORS[fuel], linewidth=2)
ax.set_xlabel('Week')
ax.set_ylabel('Mean Price (pence per litre)')
ax.set_title('Weekly Mean Fuel Price Trend — February to April 2026')
ax.legend()
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
chart7 = fig_to_base64(fig)

# Save all charts
charts = {
    'boxplot': chart1,
    'violin': chart2,
    'spread': chart3,
    'lag_hist': chart4,
    'lag_fuel': chart5,
    'coverage': chart6,
    'trend': chart7
}

import json
with open('/app/output/charts.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(charts, f)

print("Charts generated and saved to charts.json")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

df = pd.read_csv('/app/output/cleaned_data.csv')
latest = df.sort_values('recorded_at').groupby(['node_id', 'fuel_type']).last().reset_index()
main_fuels = ['E10', 'B7_STANDARD', 'E5', 'B7_PREMIUM']
main_latest = latest[latest['fuel_type'].isin(main_fuels)].copy()

# Compute exact stats for the report tables
print("=== TABLE 1: Price Distribution by Fuel Type ===")
table1 = []
for fuel in main_fuels:
    sub = main_latest[main_latest['fuel_type'] == fuel]['price_pence']
    table1.append({
        'Fuel Type': fuel,
        'Records': len(sub),
        'Mean': round(sub.mean(), 1),
        'Median': round(sub.median(), 1),
        'Std Dev': round(sub.std(), 1),
        'Min': round(sub.min(), 1),
        'Max': round(sub.max(), 1),
        'Q1': round(sub.quantile(0.25), 1),
        'Q3': round(sub.quantile(0.75), 1),
        'IQR': round(sub.quantile(0.75) - sub.quantile(0.25), 1),
        'Range': round(sub.max() - sub.min(), 1)
    })
table1_df = pd.DataFrame(table1)
print(table1_df.to_string(index=False))

print("\n=== TABLE 2: Update Freshness ===")
df['update_lag_hours'] = (pd.to_datetime(df['recorded_at']) - pd.to_datetime(df['source_updated_at'])).dt.total_seconds() / 3600
df['update_lag_hours_adj'] = df['update_lag_hours'].clip(lower=0)
table2 = []
for fuel in main_fuels:
    sub = df[df['fuel_type'] == fuel]['update_lag_hours_adj']
    table2.append({
        'Fuel Type': fuel,
        'Records': len(sub),
        'Median Lag (hrs)': round(sub.median(), 2),
        'Mean Lag (hrs)': round(sub.mean(), 1),
        'Within 1 hr (%)': round((sub <= 1).mean() * 100, 1),
        '1-24 hrs (%)': round(((sub > 1) & (sub <= 24)).mean() * 100, 1),
        '1-7 days (%)': round(((sub > 24) & (sub <= 168)).mean() * 100, 1),
        '> 7 days (%)': round((sub > 168).mean() * 100, 1)
    })
table2_df = pd.DataFrame(table2)
print(table2_df.to_string(index=False))

print("\n=== TABLE 3: Station Coverage ===")
table3 = []
for fuel in main_fuels:
    count = main_latest[main_latest['fuel_type'] == fuel]['node_id'].nunique()
    total_stations = main_latest['node_id'].nunique()
    table3.append({
        'Fuel Type': fuel,
        'Stations': count,
        'Coverage (%)': round(count / total_stations * 100, 1)
    })
table3_df = pd.DataFrame(table3)
print(table3_df.to_string(index=False))

print("\n=== TABLE 4: Station Fuel Type Availability ===")
station_fuels = main_latest.groupby('node_id')['fuel_type'].nunique()
avail = station_fuels.value_counts().sort_index()
table4 = []
for n_fuels, count in avail.items():
    table4.append({
        'Fuel Types per Station': n_fuels,
        'Station Count': count,
        'Percentage': round(count / len(station_fuels) * 100, 1)
    })
table4_df = pd.DataFrame(table4)
print(table4_df.to_string(index=False))
